canonical_statement: The study compared a fixed aPTT therapeutic range of 1.5-2.5 times control with a reagent-specific range calibrated to protamine titration heparin levels of 0.2-0.4 U/mL.
The investigation was reported as cohort studies conducted in a referral teaching hospital.
Participants were inpatients receiving intravenous unfractionated heparin for venous thromboembolic disease.

population.label: Inpatients receiving IV unfractionated heparin for venous thromboembolic disease

canonical_statement: The reference therapeutic range was defined by protamine titration heparin levels of 0.2-0.4 U/mL and compared with the conventional aPTT ratio range of 1.5-2.5 times control.

exposures.details: Ex-vivo heparin level assay used as the reference standard.

canonical_statement: Patients in studies 1 and 2 were inpatients with venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism.

population.label: Study 1 and 2 patients

canonical_statement: Patients had received continuous intravenous unfractionated heparin for at least 6 hours after a 5000 U bolus before blood sampling.
No patient was receiving warfarin at the time of blood sampling.

canonical_statement: Venous blood was collected into 3.2% buffered sodium citrate tubes.
Platelet-free plasma was prepared by sequential centrifugation and frozen at -70 degrees C for later heparin-level and aPTT testing.
Heparin levels were measured by protamine titration according to the Refn and Vestergaard method.

exposures.details: Ex-vivo heparin level assay used as the reference standard.

Study 2 additionally used the Ciba Corning 512 Monitor to determine a plasma-equivalent aPTT from whole venous blood.
Study 1 evaluated reproducibility across lots of the same Dade Actin FS reagent over a 7-year period.
Study 1 compared four Dade Actin FS lots: lot 13 (1984), lot 102 (1988), lot 129 (1991), and lot 154 (1991).

canonical_statement: For each reagent, the control value was the mean aPTT from plasma samples obtained from at least 20 hospital personnel without coagulation defects and taking no medications.
For each reagent, the relation between aPTT and simultaneously measured ex-vivo heparin level from the same plasma sample was analyzed by linear regression.

exposures.details: Ex-vivo heparin level assay used as the reference standard.

canonical_statement: Regression lines were compared by multiple linear regression, first testing slopes and then intercepts in a model constrained to a common slope.
The reagent-specific therapeutic aPTT range was defined as the regression-line aPTT values corresponding to protamine titration heparin levels of 0.2 and 0.4 U/mL.

exposures.details: Ex-vivo heparin level assay used as the reference standard.

canonical_statement: A P value below 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
Across Dade lots 13, 102, 129, and 154, regression slopes showed little evidence of nonparallelism (P > 0.2).
Across the four Dade lots, regression intercepts differed strongly (P < 0.001).
Dade lots 13, 102, and 129 had similar regression intercepts (P > 0.2).
Dade lot 154 had a regression intercept that differed from each of lots 13, 102, and 129 (P < 0.001).
Dade lot 154 differed from lot 129 despite testing duplicate plasma samples from the same 1991 patient group (P < 0.001).
Replacement Dade lots 147 and 149 produced regression lines not significantly different from lot 154.
For Ortho, Biotrack, IL, and Organon reagents, the hypothesis of parallel regression lines was rejected (P = 0.009), indicating different slopes.
For Ortho, Biotrack, IL, and Organon reagents, the regression lines were not coincident (P < 0.001), indicating differing intercepts in addition to slopes.

canonical_statement: For every aPTT reagent tested, an aPTT ratio of 1.5 corresponded to a protamine-titration heparin level below the targeted lower limit of 0.2 U/mL.

exposures.details: Ex-vivo heparin level assay used as the reference standard.

canonical_statement: A different heparin dose would be required to produce an aPTT ratio of 1.5 depending on the reagent used.
The authors considered an aPTT ratio of 1.5 subtherapeutic for all reagents tested when 0.2 U/mL by protamine titration was used as the lower reference limit.

exposures.details: Ex-vivo heparin level assay used as the reference standard.

canonical_statement: The authors cautioned that a general recommendation to target aPTT ratios of 2-3 times control could not be assured across future reagent changes or manufacturing differences.
Factor VIII and fibrinogen levels, identified as important potential confounders of the aPTT-heparin relation, were not measured and were not included in the analysis.

The authors described a four-step lot-standardization procedure: collect frozen plasma from at least 30 randomly chosen heparin-treated thrombosis patients at least 4 hours after a bolus and without warfarin; measure protamine titration heparin and aPTT with the new reagent lot; fit a least-squares regression; and define the therapeutic aPTT range at heparin levels 0.2-0.4 U/mL.

exposures.details: Ex-vivo heparin level assay used as the reference standard.

canonical_statement: Using the same manufacturer's Dade reagent over 8 years, the locally calibrated therapeutic aPTT range changed from 62-80 seconds to 79-105 seconds.
The authors preferred ex-vivo plasma from heparin-treated patients rather than plasma spiked with heparin in vitro because the aPTT-heparin relationship differs between those conditions.
The lot-specific standardization procedure may be difficult for small institutions without ready access to plasma samples from heparin-treated patients.
The authors proposed that manufacturers standardize new aPTT reagent batches and provide a therapeutic aPTT range equivalent to protamine titration heparin levels of 0.2-0.4 U/mL.

exposures.details: Ex-vivo heparin level assay used as the reference standard.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that establishing reagent-specific aPTT therapeutic ranges using protamine titration heparin levels of 0.2-0.4 U/mL is practical and compensates for variable reagent responsiveness to heparin.

exposures.details: Ex-vivo heparin level assay used as the reference standard.
